mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 1.5% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1.5% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the 60-day horizon are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) in a walk-forward test.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4% while PAYEMS increases by > 10,000 in a month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite a statistically significant positive regression coefficient for the interaction term (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% for three consecutive months indicates accelerating supply-side demand, which anticipates a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: No significant correlation between INDPRO momentum and 20-day forward returns (R-squared < 0.01, p > 0.1) in a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of industrial production to capacity (INDPRO) falls below 90 for two consecutive months, it suggests supply constraints, which typically precede a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO crosses below 90 and remains below for 2 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the identified constraint period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3% for a month triggers a preemptive rate hike by the Fed, which reduces equity valuations and produces a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3% for a month
failure_condition: No significant negative return in the 20-day window following the inflation spike (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining unemployment (UNRATE) and rising labor participation (PAYEMS) suggest a labor market transition that boosts investor sentiment, yielding positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases for 3 consecutive months while PAYEMS increases
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant positive effect from the labor transition (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of monthly new home construction (not available) — instead, use RSAFS as supply proxy: A 2-month decline in RSAFS (residential starts) suggests cooling housing market, which typically precedes a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS crosses below previous month's value and remains lower for 2 months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the cooling period.
